questions.title: Can you practise shots after finishing a hole?
questions.question: When you finish playing a hole, what kinds of practice shots are okay to do on or near the green, and where can't you practise from?

choices.text: You can practise extra putts on the green after you finish.
You can practise extra chips on or right next to the green.
You can play practice shots out of a bunker next to the green.
You can practise putting or chipping unless a sign or rule says not to.

questions.explanation: You can practise putting or chipping on or near the green after you finish the hole, as long as a sign or rule does not say you can't. But you cannot practise shots from the bunker.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The smooth, short grass area where the hole is.
A short shot that goes from just off the green onto the green.
A sand trap near the green.
A special rule given by the golf course that players must follow.

questions.teachingTip: Show different places around the green and talk about which spots you can use for practise putts and chips after a hole is finished.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking it's okay to practise from the bunker after the hole.
Forgetting to check if a local rule says no practising.

questions.title: Practising after finishing a hole
questions.question: After finishing a hole, which types of practice are allowed on the green, and where are you not allowed to practise from?

choices.text: Practising extra putts on the green.
Practising extra chips on or just beside the green.
Playing practice shots from a bunker beside the green.
Practising putts or chips unless banned by Local Rules.

questions.explanation: You may practise extra putts or chips on or near the putting green after completing a hole, unless local rules ban it. You can't practise from a bunker.
